clinical_category: Safety and Infection Prevention and Control

semantic_correction.stem: A nurse finishes contaminated wound care and must next perform a clean task for the same client. The next task also requires gloves. What should the nurse do before beginning it?

options.A: Remove the gloves, perform hand hygiene, and don a clean pair of gloves.
options.B: Keep the gloves on and clean their outer surfaces before the next task.
options.C: Remove the soiled gloves and don clean gloves without performing hand hygiene.
options.D: Keep the same gloves for the next task because care is for the same client.

semantic_correction.rationale: CDC hand-hygiene guidance directs healthcare personnel to change gloves and clean their hands when moving from a soiled body site or contaminated task to a clean body site or task on the same patient. CDC also states that gloves are not a substitute for hand hygiene. Because the next task requires gloves, the nurse should remove the contaminated gloves, perform hand hygiene, and don a clean pair. Options B and D carry contaminated gloves into clean care, and option C omits required hand hygiene after glove removal and before the next clean task.
semantic_correction.educational_objective: Prevent cross-contamination during same-client care by changing gloves and performing hand hygiene when moving from contaminated care to a clean task.
semantic_correction.source_organization: Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC)

semantic_correction.correction_summary_append: RULE1 cleanup: replaced the uniquely long correct option and absolute-word distractor pattern with four parallel same-client glove-management actions; retained the directly supported CDC contaminated-to-clean transition principle and added the exact NCSBN 2026 infection-prevention locator.

audit_findings_append.finding: The original clinical principle was correct but the answer was uniquely longest and distractors were repetitive absolutes. The revised item states that the next task requires gloves and tests the complete remove-hygiene-redon sequence without ambiguity.

option_audit.A: Correct. It completes the CDC-required glove change and hand hygiene before clean care.
option_audit.B: Incorrect. Cleaning glove surfaces does not replace removing contaminated gloves and performing hand hygiene.
option_audit.C: Incorrect. Hand hygiene is required after glove removal and before proceeding with the clean task.
option_audit.D: Incorrect. The same patient does not eliminate the need to change gloves when moving from contaminated to clean care.

ambiguity_check: No second defensible answer. A is the only option that includes both required hand hygiene and a clean pair of gloves for the next glove-requiring task.
cueing_check: Options are parallel glove-management sequences of comparable length and detail; no absolute-word or unique-length cue identifies A.
